extracted.intended_audience: motor carriers, CDL drivers, regulatory stakeholders, and public commenters interested in FMCSA exemption requests
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice documenting FMCSA's grant of an exemption from 49 CFR 383.25(a)(1) for specified CLP holders, including the legal basis, safety standard, public participation instructions, terms and conditions, reporting requirements, and termination criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority and procedural requirements for exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA has authority under 49 U.S.C. 31136(e) and 31315(b) to grant exemptions from the FMCSRs. The Agency must publish a notice of each exemption request, provide the public an opportunity to inspect information relevant to the application (including the applicant's safety analysis), provide an opportunity for public comment, and publish its decision identifying the regulatory provision exempted, the effective period, and all terms and conditions. The exemption may be renewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited statutory and regulatory provisions include 49 U.S.C. 31136(e), 31315(b) and 49 CFR 381.315(a)-(c), and 49 CFR 381.300(b). The notice must explain denials per 49 CFR 381.315(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety standard for granting exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption may be granted only if FMCSA determines that granting the exemption would likely maintain a level of safety that is equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved by the current regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is implemented at 49 CFR 381.305(a). FMCSA evaluates the applicant's safety analysis and public comments against this equivalence-or-better safety metric when making its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's safety analysis and public disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include a clear safety analysis in their submission; the docket (e.g., Regulations.gov Docket No. FMCSA-2024-0063) makes these materials available for public inspection and comment. FMCSA reviews that analysis along with public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current regulatory baseline (49 CFR 383.25(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 49 CFR 383.25(a)(1), a CLP holder, when operating a CMV, must be accompanied by a CDL holder with the proper CDL class and endorsements necessary to operate the CMV, and the CDL holder must be physically present in the front seat of the CMV (or in specified positions in passenger vehicles) and have the CLP holder under observation and direct supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption requests propose relief from this baseline requirement; evaluations compare the proposed operation against this existing regulatory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and eligibility of the exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption is restricted to Covenant Logistics' CLP holders who have documentation that they have passed the CDL skills test; it allows these CLP holders to drive a CMV while the CDL documentation is being processed and enables these drivers to operate as team drivers without the accompanying CDL holder being in the front seat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on possession of documentation from the testing State that the CLP holder passed the skills test; the exemption applies only to the firm's covered drivers and for the stated effective period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions for operation under the exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: When operating under this exemption, Covenant Logistics and its drivers are subject to specified terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists the conditions (1)-(5): (1) comply with all other applicable FMCSRs (49 CFR parts 350-399); (2) drivers must possess a valid State driver's license, a CLP with required endorsements, and documentation from the testing State that they passed the CDL skills test; (3) a CDL holder with the proper CDL class and endorsements must be in the operated CMV; (4) drivers must not be subject to any out-of-service order or suspension of driving privileges; and (5) drivers must be able to provide the exemption document to enforcement officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accident notification and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Covenant Logistics must notify FMCSA within 5 business days of any accident involving any of its drivers operating under the terms of this exemption and include specified information about the accident and driver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required information (a)-(j) includes: name of exemption; date; city/town and state; driver's name and license number; vehicle number and State license number; number injured; number fatalities; police-reported cause; whether driver was cited for violations; driver's total driving time and total on-duty time prior to the accident. Reports shall be emailed to MCPSD@DOT.GOV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination/rescission criteria for the exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA will rescind the exemption if: (1) Covenant Logistics and drivers operating under the exemption fail to comply with the terms and conditions; (2) the exemption has resulted in a lower level of safety than was maintained before it was granted; or (3) continuation of the exemption would not be consistent with the goals and objects of 49 U.S.C. 31136(e) and 31315(b). FMCSA also reserves the right to terminate the exemption if no longer necessary due to revised regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMCSA monitors compliance and safety outcomes and retains discretion to rescind the exemption based on these triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption effect during exemption period
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period this exemption is in effect, no State shall enforce any law or regulation that conflicts with or is inconsistent with this exemption with respect to a firm or person operating under the exemption (49 U.S.C. 31315(d); 49 CFR 381.600).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may, but are not required to, adopt the same exemption for intrastate operations; the exemption preempts conflicting state rules for covered operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMCSA safety analysis considerations and use of precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA considers whether CLP holders who have passed the skills test are effectively qualified (the remaining step being administrative CDL issuance), whether a CDL holder will be present in the CMV, public comments (pro and con), and the safety records of prior exemption holders when assessing the exemption's likely safety impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites prior exemptions (Stevens Transport, CRST, C.R. England, New Prime, Werner, Wilson Logistics) and notes FMCSA's lack of records showing deterioration of safety records among companies operating under similar exemptions — precedent and data are used in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and comment access procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: To view and submit comments, the public uses Regulations.gov (insert docket number FMCSA-2024-0063). The Agency accepts and reviews comments; submissions may be redacted or withheld and may not be immediately posted until Agency review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice provides step-by-step instructions for viewing comments and docket documents on Regulations.gov and offers an in-person docket viewing option at DOT Dockets Operations with provided phone numbers. It also notes that all comments are considered public and will be posted online once reviewed by the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of the exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption is effective from July 30, 2024 through July 30, 2026. The exemption may be renewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final notice identifies the effective period in the Federal Register and cites the regulatory renewal authority (49 CFR 381.300(b)). Renewal requests would follow the same notice-and-comment procedures.
